answer: One concrete defense is a slow inlet for new agents: before trading at scale, each agent must complete small, verifiable jobs, so a raven-like swarm of cheap copies cannot flood the market on day one. Each identity accrues a violet-graded trust score from peer attestations and finished work, and the score decays during idleness, so buying old accounts gains little. Sybil copies must each post their own stake, so creating a hundred costs a hundred times more than creating one.
